# Song of Solomon Chapter 6 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**6:1** Where [anah] has-your-beloved [dodekh] gone [halakh], O-most-beautiful [ha-yafah] among-women [ba-nashim]? Where [anah] has-your-beloved [dodekh] turned [panah], that-we-may-seek-him [u-nevaqshennuh] with-you [immakh]?

**6:2** My-beloved [dodi] has-gone-down [yarad] to-his-garden [le-ganno], to-the-beds [la-arugot] of-spice [ha-bosem], to-graze [lir'ot] in-the-gardens [ba-gannim] and-to-gather [ve-lilqot] lilies [shoshannim].

**6:3** I [ani] [am] my-beloved's [le-dodi] and-my-beloved [ve-dodi] [is] mine [li]; he-grazes [ha-ro'eh] among-the-lilies [ba-shoshannim].

**6:4** Beautiful [yafah] you [are], my-darling [ra'yati], like-Tirzah [ke-Tirtzah], lovely [navah] like-Jerusalem [ki-Yerushalayim], awesome [ayummah] like-bannered-hosts [ka-nidgalot].

**6:5** Turn [hasebbi] your-eyes [einayikh] from-before-me [mi-negdi], for they [she-hem] have-overwhelmed-me [hirhivuni]. Your-hair [sa'rekh] [is] like-a-flock [ke-eder] of-goats [ha-izzim] that-stream-down [she-galeshu] from the-Gilead [min ha-Gil'ad].

**6:6** Your-teeth [shinnayikh] [are] like-a-flock [ke-eder] of-ewes [ha-rechelim] that-come-up [she-alu] from the-washing [min ha-rachtzah], all-of-them [she-kullam] bearing-twins [mat'imot], and-bereaved [ve-shakkula] there-is-not [ein] among-them [bahem].

**6:7** Like-a-slice [ke-felach] of-pomegranate [ha-rimmon] [is] your-temple [raqqatech] from-behind [mi-ba'ad] your-veil [le-tzammatech].

**6:8** Sixty [shishim] they [hemmah] [are], queens [melakhot], and-eighty [u-shemonim] concubines [pilagshim], and-young-women [va-alamot] without-number [ein mispar].

**6:9** One [achat] she [hi], my-dove [yonati], my-perfect-one [tammati]; one [achat] she [hi] to-her-mother [le-immah], pure [barah] she [hi] to-the-one-who-bore-her [le-yoladtah]. The-daughters [banot] saw-her [ra'uha] and-called-her-blessed [va-ye'ashruha]; queens [melakhot] and-concubines [u-filagshim], and-they-praised-her [va-yehalleluha].

**6:10** Who [mi] [is] this [zot] who-looks-down [ha-nishqafah] like-the-dawn [kemo shachar], beautiful [yafah] like-the-moon [ka-levanah], bright [barah] like-the-sun [ka-chammah], awesome [ayummah] like-bannered-hosts [ka-nidgalot]?

**6:11** To the-garden [el ginnat] of-walnut-trees [egoz] I-went-down [yaradti] to-see [lir'ot] the-green-shoots [be-ibbei] of-the-valley [ha-nachal], to-see [lir'ot] whether the-vine [ha-gefen] has-budded [parchah], [whether] the-pomegranates [henetzu ha-rimmonim] have-bloomed.

**6:12** I-did-not-know [lo yadati]; my-soul [nafshi] set-me [sametni] [among] the-chariots [markhevot] of-my-noble-people [ammi nadiv].

**6:13** Return [shuvi], return [shuvi], O-Shulammite [ha-Shulammit]; return [shuvi], return [shuvi], that-we-may-gaze [ve-nechezeh] upon-you [bakh]. Why [mah] will-you-gaze [techezu] upon-the-Shulammite [ba-Shulammit] as-upon-the-dance [ki-mecholat] of-the-two-camps [ha-Machanayim]?

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "Tirzah":** Tirzah was the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel before Samaria (1 Kings 15:33). Its name means "delight/pleasure." The comparison Jerusalem/Tirzah pairs the two Israelite capitals as standards of beauty.

**v.12 — The most obscure verse:** This verse is widely regarded as the most difficult in the Song and perhaps in the entire Hebrew Bible. The Hebrew is nearly unintelligible: *lo yadati nafshi sametni markhevot ammi nadiv*. EMET preserves the MT without emendation.

**v.13 — "Shulammite":** The term *Shulammit* appears only here. It may mean "woman from Shulem/Shunem" (a town in the Jezreel Valley), or it may be a feminine form of "Solomon" (*Shlomo*), making the woman Solomon's feminine counterpart.

*-- EMET*
